svg.title: Elasticity measures how relative input error is amplified
svg.desc: Absolute sensitivity uses f'(x) . Relative sensitivity uses the dimensionless factor E(x)=x f'(x)/f(x) , which predicts the approximate percentage output change caused by a one-percent input change. The first box measures error as a fraction of the input rather than in raw units. Elasticity multiplies that fraction. The result is a fractional output error, so the comparison works across quantities with different units and scales. Large |E(x)| warns that small relative input errors may be strongly amplified.
